== Biography ==
=== Irish family roles, 24 October 2026 ===

Father [[Glasgow-1025|James]], specifically the James/Margaret Rutherford family-account role: [[Glasgow-1024|James]] 18%→78%, [[Glasgow-1492|Samuel]] 23%→76%, [[Glasgow-2425|Robert]] 18%→77%, [[Glasgow-2426|William]] 46%→84%, all now probable. The American [[Glasgow-12|Robert]]/[[Glasgow-649|Arthur]]/[[Glasgow-1543|Joseph]] father grades remain35%, [[Glasgow-4027|John]] remains30%, [[Glasgow-4030|Mary]] remains22%; [[Glasgow-1025|James]]’s own [[Glasgow-1026|William]] father remains32%. The anonymous family recollection printed by Faris on p.9 explicitly gives James Glasgow, husband of Margaret Rutherford, four sons: William, Robert, James who settled near Moneymore, and Samuel who went to America, plus daughter Ellen. The letter-defined father is the family role represented by [[Glasgow-1025|James]]. These are specific named relationships, substantially stronger than the contributed-tree and locality summaries used by the earlier percentages. The same full-letter tradition was already read on 20 October; actual Faris pages now confirm its full structure. Its reproduction by Albert Rutherford and Faris’s pedigree are dependent presentations, not independent witnesses. [[Glasgow-2425|Robert]] is the inherited James/Margaret Rutherford son account, matching the letter’s named Robert, himself described as a William Glasgow’s father. This specific position in the named sibling family supports 77%, while his adult life remains little anchored. His imported United States death location is not established by the letter or by the will’s Ireland designation. These are probable, not confident, relationships reconstructed from an anonymous retrospective family recollection, with no newly inspected parent register. The original letter remains uninspected. Faris calls the anonymous recollection file5 within PRONI T1959, while Rutherford’s reproduced copy cites T1959/3; retain this reference discrepancy pending archive checking. The 1759 probate index says Drumcarn and names no kin; neither that testator nor the inherited life dates are identified by this reassessment. The letter calls William eldest although the imported sibling birth estimates put him later; those estimates remain unverified. Faris also flags Samuel’s infant daughter and surviving mother-in-law in1824 against the supposed early paternal death. Those tensions require testing, not automatic exclusion. Preserve all existing people, vital fields, maternal grades and alternatives. No Scottish migration, identity merge, live edit or new father attachment is claimed.<ref>David Faris, The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio(1990), printed pp.8–12; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9VW-J pp.8–9], [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3J-H9VW-9 pp.12–13], DGS007834162, images1564–1566. PRONI T1959 anonymous family recollection, in [https://www.genealogy.com/forum/surnames/topics/rutherford/5445/ Albert Rutherford’s reproduction]; original letter uninspected. Chester County estate7520, [https://portal.laserfiche.com/Portal/DocView.aspx?id=773006&page=588&repo=r-24f48cc6 original will, pp588–589], previously inspected23October2026.</ref>


Robert is currently recorded as born about 1724 and attached as a son of [[Glasgow-1025|James Glasgow]] and [[Rutherford-4861|Margaret Rutherford]]. The only cited basis is a user-contributed FamilySearch tree; no inspected original record yet proves his birth, parents, migration or death.

Source basis already held: [https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/MCTD-7P4 FamilySearch Family Tree, MCTD-7P4 (https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/MCTD-7P4); user-contributed tree, used only as a lead.]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


=== Moneymore place conflict ===

The structured birthplace “Moneymore, County Galway” combines a real place-name with a county that does not fit the Moneymore used in this family reconstruction. Moneymore in Artrea civil parish is in County Londonderry, not County Galway.<ref>[https://www.townlands.ie/londonderry/loughinsholin/artrea/moneymore/moneymore/ Townlands.ie, “Moneymore Townland, Co. Londonderry”], placing Moneymore in Artrea civil parish, barony of Loughinsholin, County Londonderry.</ref> This geographic correction does '''not''' prove that Robert was born in the Londonderry townland: several Irish places share the name, and no record inspected for Robert identifies one of them.

PRONI's official church-register guide lists First Moneymore Presbyterian baptisms only from 1827, Second Moneymore from 1845, and Ardtrea/Desertlin Roman Catholic baptisms from 1832.<ref>[https://www.proni.gov.uk/publications/proni-guide-church-records Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, ''Guide to Church Records''], First Moneymore Presbyterian MIC1P/339; Second Moneymore Presbyterian MIC1P/340; Ardtrea/Desertlin MIC1D/35 and T3050; guide consulted 30 August 2026.</ref> None of those surviving series can record a birth about 1724. This explains the register gap but does not prove Robert's identity, birthplace or parents; deeds, estate papers, probate and other contemporary records remain the appropriate next search.

The current parents, sibling group, birth and death locations are retained until evidence supplies replacements. They should be treated as unproved tree claims, as noted in [[Space:Glasgow Branches in Early Ireland|Glasgow Branches in Early Ireland]], rather than silently cleared or converted into a different family.

=== Possible Robert Glasgow, Cecil County plantation notice, 1786 ===
A notice dated North Susquehanna hundred, Cecil county, Maryland, 10 February 1786 offers a 260-acre plantation for public vendue on 10 March, with immediate possession given by Robert Glasgow and Joshua Hartshorn.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/41024006/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1786-02-15, p.1].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/41024088/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1786-03-01, p.4].</ref>

The two issues advertise one planned sale. Robert’s role as owner, agent or another participant is not specified; the notice proves neither a completed sale nor kinship with Joshua Hartshorn.

This may concern [[Glasgow-2425]]. Estimated birth c. 1724 in Ireland and death place United States leave the chronology possible, but the known account gives no Maryland residence or relevant occupation. The identification is therefore weak.
